topic: Rate analysis, contracts, norms, labour/material rates, contractor terms

questions.q: 35. Generally the provision for supervision is
questions.explain: Work supervision charges are typically estimated at 5% to 10% of the total cost.

questions.q: 37. Excavation of earth work analysis is done
questions.explain: Rate analysis for excavation includes both labor (manpower) and mechanical equipment (plant).

questions.q: 45. Unit rate is only for
questions.explain: According to the key, unit rates are used for preparing documents (like tender documents).

questions.q: 56. Normally which one contract gives the maximum value of project
questions.explain: An item rate contract often leads to a higher project value as every individual unit of work is measured and paid for based on actual execution.

questions.q: 96. *The rate analysis induces
options: material, labour, contractor's overhead and profit
questions.explain: Comprehensive rate analysis must account for materials, labor, overheads, and the contractor's profit margin.

questions.q: 97. The overheads and profit claimed by the contractor to client is
questions.explain: These costs are not billed separately but are embedded into the unit rates of the work items.

questions.q: 99. *The main target of a contractor is to
questions.explain: While a contractor must complete the work, the primary business objective is to maximize profit.

questions.q: 100. *The chairman of material rate fixation committee in district is
questions.explain: In the Nepalese administrative system, the Chief District Officer (CDO) chairs the committee that fixes district material rates.

questions.q: 101. Rate analysis prepared by ministry of transport and work includes
questions.explain: According to the MOPIT (Ministry of Physical Infrastructure and Transport) norms, rate analysis comprehensively includes the cost of labour, materials, and necessary equipment/machinery for the task.

questions.q: 102. *Full payment of contractor is done
questions.explain: Full and final payment is released only after the 'Defects Liability Period' or maintenance period is over to ensure all construction defects are rectified.

questions.q: 103. As per norms prepared by MOPIT the number of skilled and unskilled manpower required to dismantling of existing structure having conc. grade M10 for 20 m3
questions.explain: Official MOPIT norms specify 3 skilled and 30 unskilled laborers for dismantling 15 cubic meters of M15 concrete structure.

questions.q: 104. In sanitary pipe line for 3m length, how many skilled labour are required
questions.explain: Higher grade concrete (M20) requires more effort; the norms specify 3 skilled and 30 unskilled workers for this volume.

questions.q: 105. As per norms prepared by MOPIT, the of brick on edge required for footpath on 60 mm thick sand bed for 10 m2
questions.explain: For brick-on-edge paving on a 60mm sand bed, 825 bricks are required for a 10 square meter area.

questions.q: 106. As per norms prepared by MOPIT, the of brick on flat required for footpath on 60 mm thick sand bed for 20 m2
questions.explain: For flat brick paving, the requirement is 750 bricks per 20 square meters according to MOPIT standards.

questions.q: 107. The expected out turn of brick work in cement mortar (1:6) in foundation and plinth per mason per day (as per MOPIT norms), is
questions.explain: The standard daily output (out-turn) for a mason doing brickwork in the foundation/plinth is 0.83 cubic meters.

questions.q: 108. The no. of masons required per cubic metre of DRY stone masonry (as per MOPIT norms), is
questions.explain: Dry stone masonry is labor-intensive; 0.8 masons are required per cubic meter.

questions.q: 109. The no. of skilled man power required per cubic metre cement concrete 1:2:4 (as per MOPIT norms), is
questions.explain: For mixing and placing 1:2:4 concrete, the skilled labor coefficient is 0.2 per cubic meter.

questions.q: 110. The no. of skilled manpower required for 10 m2 plaster having thickness 12.5mm in 1:2 mortar (as per MOPIT norms), is
questions.explain: For 10m2 of 12.5mm thick plaster (1:2 ratio), 10 skilled manpower units are required.

questions.q: 111. The no. of skilled manpower required for 10 m2 plaster having thickness 12.5mm in 1:3 mortar (as per MOPIT norms), is
questions.explain: The norm specifies 12 skilled manpower units for 10m2 of 1:3 ratio plaster at 12.5mm thickness.

questions.q: 112. In RCC work, one mason in one day can perform
questions.explain: In reinforced cement concrete (RCC) work, the out-turn per mason is relatively low (0.20 m3) due to the complexity of working around reinforcement.

questions.q: 113. The quantity of thermoplastic paint for 400 m2 on smooth road surface (as per MOPIT norms), is
questions.explain: MOPIT norms state that 930 liters of thermoplastic paint are needed for a 400m2 smooth road surface.

questions.q: 114. The quantity of thermoplastic paint for 300 m2 on smooth road surface (as per MOPIT norms), is
questions.explain: The requirement for 300m2 is listed as 1200 liters in the provided key.

questions.q: 120. *The number of skilled manpower required for fabrication of 1MT steel is
questions.explain: Fabricating one metric ton (MT) of reinforcement steel typically requires 12 skilled workers.

questions.q: 133. The portion which is wrongly excavated by the contractor is to be filled
options: the earth excavated from the same pit
the earth excavated from a borrow pit for away from the site
questions.explain: If a contractor over-excavates foundation trenches, they must fill the excess with concrete to ensure structural integrity.

questions.q: 134. In the analysis of rates what percentage of total cost is provided towards water charges
questions.explain: A standard allowance of 1.5% of the total cost is added to cover water charges used during construction.

questions.q: 138. *Steel formwork can be used upto about.........times.
questions.explain: Due to its durability, steel formwork can be reused approximately 50 times with proper maintenance.

questions.q: 157. If valuable properties are found during excavation, it becomes the property of
questions.explain: Standard contract clauses (and the Treasure Trove Act) stipulate that any fossils, coins, or articles of value found during excavation belong to the Government.

questions.q: 168. In the analysis of rates, the profit and over head for the contractor is generally taken as
questions.explain: As per standard norms (including Nepal's norms), 15% is added to the cost of materials and labor to cover contractor overheads and profit.

questions.q: 169. Contractor tax is
questions.explain: In many South Asian public procurement systems, a 1.5% TDS (Tax Deducted at Source) is applied to the contractor's bills.

questions.q: 177. Tender does not contain
questions.explain: A blank tender provided to a contractor contains items and quantities but not the rates; the contractor fills in the rates.

questions.q: 178. The amount of money deposited along with the submission of tender is known as
questions.explain: earnest money or bid security is deposited while bidding.

questions.q: 194. A fixed stipulated sum of penalty payable by the contractor having no relationship with real damage, is known as
questions.explain: Liquidated damages are pre-estimated amounts fixed in the contract to be paid if a breach (like delay) occurs.

questions.q: 195. Liquidated damage is directly related with
questions.explain: Liquidated damages are governed by the specific clauses and terms of the contract agreement.

questions.q: 196. A fixed stipulated sum of penalty payable by the contractor having certain relationship with real damage, is known as
questions.explain: Unliquidated damages are not fixed in the contract and are determined by a court based on the actual loss suffered.

questions.q: 197. When engineering departments undertake the works of other departments the amount charged toward design, supervision and execution etc. is called
questions.explain: Centage charges (or departmental charges) are fees collected by a construction department for services rendered to another department.

questions.q: 198. Work charged establishment
questions.explain: A provision of 1.5% to 2% is typically made in the estimate for staff (supervisors, etc.) employed specifically for that project.

questions.q: 200. Which of the following is known as job overhead?
questions.explain: Job overheads are expenses directly related to a specific project site, such as insurance for workers and site-specific supervision.

questions.q: 201. In which of the following works, the work turned in cu.m per mason per day will be the least
options: random rubble masonry in lime mortar
questions.explain: Stone arch work requires high precision, dressing, and complex centering, which significantly reduces the daily output (outturn) per mason compared to straight walling.

questions.q: 202. Which of the following is known as general overhead?
questions.explain: General overheads include expenses that cannot be charged to a specific job, such as office rent, administrative salaries, and traveling expenses for general business.

questions.q: 206. Actual Cost of construction plus certain profit is paid to the contractor . such a contract is known as
questions.explain: In a cost-plus-percentage contract, the contractor is reimbursed the actual verified cost of construction plus an agreed percentage as profit.

questions.q: 207. When contractor fails to complete the work, an agency is employed to execute a part or whole of the at the cost of contractor. Such an agency is known as
questions.explain: A debitable agency is hired to complete unfinished work, and the costs incurred are debited (charged) to the original contractor's account.

questions.q: 211. The document showing the account of work done or supply of material including the particulars and quantities is known as
questions.explain: A bill is a formal statement of account showing the amount due for work performed or materials supplied.

questions.q: 212. The full form of VAT is
questions.explain: VAT stands for Value Added Tax, which is a consumption tax placed on a product whenever value is added at each stage of the supply chain.

questions.q: 218. Rate analysis is based on the following factors
questions.explain: Analysis of rates considers the quantity of materials, their quality, current market rates, and labor costs to determine the unit price of an item.

questions.q: 225. The amount provisioned for tools and plants on earthwork excavation item in norms for rate analysis is:
questions.explain: Tools and plants (T&P) charges are often estimated as a percentage of the labor cost for manual excavation.

questions.q: 234. Which of the following is not a part of estimating norms for rate analysis?
questions.explain: Standard rate analysis focuses on direct costs (labor, material, equipment); taxes like VAT are usually added at the summary level, not within individual item norms.

questions.q: 235. What is the defects liability period in construction norms for rate analysis?
questions.explain: The standard defects liability period (DLP) for most construction contracts is typically one year after completion.

questions.q: 240. The main purpose of rate analysis is:
options: to find actual cost per unit items
to find economic value of material
both a and B of the above
questions.explain: The primary goal is to determine the unit rate of a work item based on its components.

questions.q: 243. The provision for overhead and profit in the rate analysis is generally:
questions.explain: The standard allowance for contractor's profit and overhead combined is generally taken as 15%.

questions.q: 245. FIDIC is
questions.explain: FIDIC (Fédération Internationale Des Ingénieurs-Conseils) is the International Federation of Consulting Engineers.

questions.q: 248. Key components of norms prepared for rate analysis of works may not include with quantity of
questions.explain: Establishment costs (overhead) are added as a percentage, not as a specific quantity component in the base norms.

questions.q: 249. The rates worked for material/labour based on paid bills/vouchers produced by contractor plus profit is
questions.explain: Star rates are rates derived from actual market prices plus profit when the item is not in the standard schedule of rates.
